title: No image generator at all: our AI agents draw pixel art as code, light it with a dithered palette pass, and render their own trailer
author: RemoteTime9538
selftext:
Iut is a short cozy game about an apartment block in a blackout. It's made with Claude Code agents on our own Rust/wasm engine, and the process might interest this sub more than the game itself.

What we do differently:

* Art as code, not as images. Agents write sprites and scenes as code against one 36-colour palette. Nothing is generated by an image model, so every pixel can be changed by asking for a code change, and the style stays consistent across characters.
* Light as a palette pass. The blackout is a dithered lighting pass (torch, candles, windows coming back floor by floor) rather than painted dark versions of the art.
* Sound in code. Every sound is synthesized: footsteps, doors, a Karplus-Strong guitar, a choir.
* Agents check their own work. Headless tests play a whole evening; a browser script plays it with real mouse and touch input in Firefox and saves screenshots for review.
* The trailer is code too. Each shot is staged in Rust from the game's own assets and rendered for 16:9 and 9:16, so the trailer can never drift from the game.

A human (me) decides the design and says no a lot. Free to play: [https://seongames.itch.io/iut](https://seongames.itch.io/iut)

Curious how others here handle art consistency without image models.

comments.body:
its still generative AI, its still AI generated art that faces the player    

Having the ai generate images, or having it generate code that draws the images it generated is the same thing, and its amounts to the same disclosure.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: One of the things I've enjoyed about carefully setting up a rig so that my LLM could easily make a videos from headless game play, was eventually having it scoped out enough to end a day of vibe coding with "Take all the new features we made today and amend them to the existing trailer showing off the new functionality"
